title: Invoice Export
tagline: Bookkeepers get every invoice out of Fieldnote in one click, in their tool's format.

round.title: PDF bundles and the monthly send

needs.text: Invite the build bot to the staging account so wave 4 can run the walk
Wave 3 starts after the wave 2 gate, about Thursday

problem.statement: Every month our customers' bookkeepers copy invoices out of Fieldnote by hand. They rebuild a spreadsheet, download PDFs one at a time, and email them on. It takes hours and the totals often drift.
today: 41 support tickets in September asked for an export
PDFs download one at a time, about 4 seconds each
Nobody can see who took which invoices out

quotes.text: I spend the first Monday of every month copying numbers between two tabs.
Make it one button. My bookkeeper should never need to log in.

outcomes.claim: A bookkeeper exports a month of invoices as one CSV that imports into their accounting tool with no edits.
done_when: The CSV imports cleanly into the three tools we support
Totals match the invoice list to the cent

outcomes.claim: Anyone with the finance role downloads a zip of PDFs for any date range, 2,000 invoices in under 30 seconds.
done_when: 2,000 invoices zip in under 30 seconds on staging
Every PDF in the zip matches the one on screen

outcomes.claim: An owner sets a monthly export once, and it lands in the bookkeeper's inbox on the day they chose.
done_when: A test schedule sends on the chosen day in the account's time zone

outcomes.claim: Every export is recorded with who ran it, when, and which invoices left.
done_when: The export history shows every run, including scheduled ones

findings.finding: Bookkeepers rebuild the spreadsheet by hand every month.
findings.solution: One CSV with presets for the three tools our customers use most.

findings.finding: PDFs render on the web server, about 4 seconds each, one at a time.
findings.solution: Render in a background worker, 8 at a time, and cache each PDF by invoice version.

findings.finding: There is no record of who downloaded which invoices.
findings.solution: Every export writes one row: who, when, filters and invoice count.

findings.finding: Date filters use UTC, so month ends drift for customers in the Americas.
findings.solution: Filter by the account's own time zone everywhere exports run.

research.question: What CSV layout do the accounting tools our customers use actually import?
research.answer: All three accept one row per invoice with a fixed set of columns. Two of them also accept one row per line item, which bookkeepers prefer for tax splits.
recommendations: Ship one row per invoice as the default
Offer line items as a preset, not a setting

research.question: How do we render 2,000 PDFs in under 30 seconds?
research.answer: A worker pool of 8 renders about 90 PDFs a second once warm. Caching by invoice version removes most of the work for repeat exports.
recommendations: Move rendering to a queue worker
Cache PDFs by invoice id and version

research.question: Do bookkeepers want the monthly export by email or in a shared folder?
research.answer: Email, by a wide margin. They forward it into their own systems and do not want another login.
recommendations: Email a link that expires after 7 days

architecture.summary: Exports run as background jobs so the web app stays fast. Each job writes a record, renders what it needs, and hands the file to storage or email.

plan.summary: We build exports as background jobs in four waves of parallel agents. CSV and the job runner come first, then PDF bundles, then the monthly send. Every ticket proves itself with a test and a screenshot before the gate.

principles.title: Jobs, not requests
principles.text: Anything over a second runs as a job with a record.

principles.title: Presets over settings
principles.text: Bookkeepers pick their tool; we pick the columns.

principles.title: Account time zone
principles.text: Every date range uses the account's own zone.

done_when: 500 PDFs render in under 8 seconds warm

waves.why: Each builds on one wave 2 piece.

waves.why: Joins everything and proves it on staging.

Browser walk of what the wave changed
Lead spot check of one proof

stop_rules: A blocking decision is still not opened
The baseline goes red and one fix does not bring it back
A review finding survives three rounds

verification.what: Its own test command and a screenshot of the result
Full test suite, two fresh reviews, and a browser walk of the wave
A recorded walk on staging data

plan.commits: One commit per ticket on the draft PR branch, message names the ticket title.

risks.risk: Accounting tools change their import format
risks.mitigation: Presets live in one file with a test per tool
Stream the zip and cap the range

decisions.question: Where does the Export button live?
decisions.why: The dialog ticket cannot finish until we know where people start an export.

options.label: Invoice list toolbar
options.effect: Found in one click. Ticket stays as planned.

options.label: Settings page
options.effect: Quieter list. Adds a link from the list, same wave.

decisions.question: Which CSV layout is the default?
decisions.why: Two of three tools accept both; bookkeepers split tax by line.

options.label: One row per line item
options.effect: Better for tax splits. One tool needs a preset.

decisions.question: When does the monthly export send?
decisions.why: Bookkeepers close the month on different days.

options.label: A day the owner picks
options.effect: Adds one field to the schedule settings.

decisions.question: What is the most invoices in one zip?
decisions.why: Bigger zips risk timeouts on slow connections.

options.effect: Covers everyone. Needs streaming, already planned.

options.label: No cap
options.effect: Adds a risk of timeouts. Not advised.

kickoff: Build Invoice Export, round 3. Read the book at https://claude.ai/artifact/example-invoice-export (agent/book.json and agent/CHECKPOINT.md first). Run waves 2 to 4 as planned, one builder per ticket, each proving its own done-when with a test and a screenshot. Write status, run and log rows as you go. Stop and ask in chat if a blocking decision is still not opened.
